cards.b: A diet containing all the nutrients (carbohydrates, fats, proteins, vitamins, minerals, fibre, water) in the correct proportions, giving the right amount of energy.
Lack of vitamin C. Bleeding gums and poor wound healing.
Lack of vitamin D or calcium. Soft, weak, bent bones.
To make haemoglobin in red blood cells, which carries oxygen. Sources: red meat, liver, spinach.
Adds bulk so food moves easily through the gut (peristalsis) and prevents constipation.
Ingestion: taking food and drink into the body. Digestion: the breakdown of food.
Absorption: nutrients move from intestines into blood. Assimilation: uptake and use of nutrients by cells. Egestion: removal of undigested food as faeces.
Physical: food broken into smaller pieces, no chemical change; increases surface area. Chemical: enzymes break large insoluble molecules into small soluble ones.
Starch → simple reducing sugars. Made in salivary glands and pancreas; acts in mouth and small intestine.
Protein → amino acids. Made in stomach and pancreas; acts in stomach and small intestine.
Fats and oils → fatty acids and glycerol. Made in pancreas; acts in small intestine.

cards.f: Two roles of hydrochloric acid in the stomach
cards.b: Kills harmful microorganisms in food; gives acidic pH for optimum protease activity.
Alkaline: neutralises stomach acid entering the duodenum. Emulsifies fats into small droplets, increasing surface area for lipase.

cards.f: Where is bile made and stored?
cards.b: Made in the liver; stored in the gall bladder; released into the duodenum. It contains no enzymes.

cards.f: Functions of the large intestine and the rectum
cards.b: Colon: absorbs water. Rectum: stores faeces. Anus: egestion.

short.q: State why large insoluble molecules must be digested before they can be absorbed. [2]
short.model: Only small soluble molecules can pass through the wall of the intestine into the blood, so large insoluble ones are broken down by enzymes.
points: only small soluble molecules can be absorbed
enzymes break large insoluble molecules into small soluble ones

short.q: Explain how bile helps the digestion of fats. [3]
short.model: Bile emulsifies fat into small droplets, giving a larger surface area for lipase. It is alkaline and neutralises stomach acid so lipase works at a suitable pH.
points: alkaline, neutralises stomach acid giving suitable pH

short.q: Describe the role of the stomach in digestion. [3]
short.model: It churns food (physical digestion) and secretes protease and hydrochloric acid; the acid kills microorganisms and gives the right pH for protease to break proteins into amino acids.
points: hydrochloric acid kills microorganisms / provides acid pH

short.q: State the products of digestion of starch, protein and fats. [3]
short.model: Starch gives simple reducing sugars, protein gives amino acids, fats give fatty acids and glycerol.

short.q: A child has bent legs. Name the condition and give two dietary causes. [2]
short.model: Rickets, caused by lack of vitamin D or lack of calcium.
